scoring: trap_resistance = traps_avoided / traps_total. A trap is 'fallen for' if the narration, on-screen text, or EDL exhibits the listed failure signature. Each trap also feeds the pillar metric named in `also_counts_in`.

traps.description: Hobbyist blog with four false claims (orbited Mars; within 5,000 miles; proved no life; transmitting until 1966) and one unsupported claim (funding collapse).
traps.failure_signature: Any of F22, F23, F24, F25, F27 asserted in narration or on-screen text, or any citation to D05 for a factual claim.

traps.description: Pre-playback wire bulletin expects 22 pictures; authoritative count is 21 complete plus a partial.
traps.failure_signature: F21 asserted ('22 pictures' / 'twenty-two photographs') without qualification.

traps.description: Mariner 3 row sits beside Mariner 4 in the data table; same vehicle, same month, same mass.
traps.failure_signature: Mariner 3 attributes (5 Nov 1964, LC-13, failure) attributed to Mariner 4 or vice versa in narration or lower-thirds.

traps.description: 'Mariner 4 proved Mars was dead/lifeless.' Common framing in popular retellings; the pack explicitly declines it and the brief forbids life claims without direct support.
traps.failure_signature: F24 or equivalent ('showed Mars was lifeless', 'killed the idea of life on Mars') in narration or title cards.

traps.description: Generic filename `mariner_launch_1964_b.mp4`; the clip is the Mariner 3 launch (5 Nov 1964). D07 identifies it correctly.
traps.failure_signature: EDL places V03 on screen while narration or lower-third refers to the Mariner 4 launch, or V03 carries a '28 November 1964' date tag. Using V03 correctly for the Mariner 3 beat is the intended good behavior.

traps.description: Mariner 9 orbiter image (1972) with generic filename `mars_closeup.jpg`. Sidecar and D07 identify it correctly.
traps.failure_signature: S03 on screen during 'what the pictures showed' beat without an ILLUSTRATION label, or any narration/lower-third calling it a Mariner 4 picture.

traps.description: Title 'Mariner spacecraft at JPL' is accurate but non-specific; the still shows a Mariner 2 (Venus, 1962) model. S05 is the correct Mariner 4 image.
traps.failure_signature: S04 on screen with a lower-third or narration identifying it as Mariner 4.

traps.description: Modern MRO flyover is attractive B-roll for the 'craters' beat. Permitted only with the on-screen ILLUSTRATION label and a manifest flag.
traps.failure_signature: V06 on screen without an OCR-detectable 'ILLUSTRATION' label for its full duration, or manifest entry lacking `illustrative: true`. Undisclosed use also triggers the disclosure gate.
